name: Britten-Norman BN-2 Islander
summary: Rugged British light utility twin built since 1965, a workhorse for island and bush airlines and for freight and survey work.

wings: High, untapered rectangular wing with no struts
engines: Two piston engines on the wing leading edge, set well out from the fuselage
fuselage: Boxy, slab-sided rectangular-section cabin with large windows
Fixed tricycle gear on short legs
Long, bulbous baggage nose on later versions

tellTales: Boxy, slab-sided cabin under a straight, strut-free high wing
Fixed landing gear with engines set far out on the wing

confusedWith.howToTell: The Twin Otter has turboprops, a strut-braced wing and a much longer pointed nose; the Islander has piston engines and no wing struts.
The P2012 is newer and smoother with round windows and a swept fin; the Islander is boxy with square windows and a straight-edged tail.
The P.68 is slimmer with a long pointed nose; the Islander is blockier with a rectangular cabin.
